analysis.title: The Day Ahead - For Tuesday, November 17, 2026
key_insights: US stocks fell broadly on Monday after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO. The Dow lost 1.41% to 51,608.17, the S&P 500 lost 1.92% to 7,416.59 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 2.49% to 24,509.76. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 5.28% to 9,610.65.

Nvidia reports Q3 results Tuesday after the close, with a revenue estimate of about $109.1B and an EPS estimate of $2.48 (LSEG IBES). Attention has moved from margin and cash-use questions to Nvidia's influence across the AI ecosystem and who will lead the company. Colette Kress is interim CEO.

Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back, per three people who spoke to Reuters. A petition for his return has more than 180,200 signatures, with support from Elon Musk and President Trump. Governance experts and some investors warn that reinstating him before the investigations finish could expose the company to new risks.

US intelligence agencies are still working out how far Alice Huang's relationship with China's Ministry of State Security went. Sources say the evidence so far suggests she was likely an intelligence asset who shared information, not a fully trained spy.

Nvidia's $500B AI financing platform is expected to continue under Kress. Analysts expect an initial pause, and they worry about less appetite for riskier infrastructure bets, including Nvidia's investments in AI startups and neoclouds.

Baird's Ross Mayfield describes day-to-day swings between AI names and a rotation trade. He sees signs that investors are probing other corners of the equity market, not leaving the asset class. Anthropic's IPO later this week adds to the stakes for AI sentiment.

Portfolio managers are trying to measure how much AI risk sits in their portfolios. At least $25.3T is invested in the largest global companies with the most direct AI exposure, per the MSCI Global Intelligence Index.

Treasury yields eased on a modest safe-haven bid after two-year yields posted their biggest weekly jump in two years on Friday. The 10-year yield closed at 5.1311%, the 2-year at 4.8315%, the 5-year at 4.9418% and the 30-year at 5.4763%.

The dollar index rose 0.18% to 103.60, supported by last week's strong inflation data and hawkish Fed commentary. The report's lead says the dollar is at its highest against a basket of currencies since April 2025. Macro Hive's Benjamin Ford sees EUR/USD at 1.08 as achievable into year-end. The euro fell 0.24% and sterling fell 0.29% to $1.3177.

Gold fell on a stronger dollar and expectations of a Fed rate hike next month. Spot gold touched $3,830, its lowest since October 2025. A Reuters graphic says gold is heading for its worst year since 2015. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was due to speak.

Oil fell as signs of recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz reinforced expectations of surplus supply. Fresh tanker incidents still point to risks for Middle East exports. WTI fell 3.40% to $85.55 and Brent fell 3.60% to $92.39.

Tyson Foods rose 8.74% to $63.96 after beating estimates (adjusted EPS of 61 cents vs 58 cents expected). Its fiscal 2027 adjusted operating income guidance is $1.7B to $2.15B against $1.98B in fiscal 2026. It expects a meaningful improvement in beef, with a result between a $300M adjusted loss and a $100M adjusted profit versus a $654M loss in 2026.

A Friday FAA nationwide ground stop caused more than 18,500 flight cancellations as of Monday morning. Bernstein estimates a combined pretax hit of about $345M to American, Delta, United and Southwest, with an 80% range of $270M to $430M. American and JetBlue were slowest to recover, cancelling 22% and 28% of Sunday flights.

Fed Chair Warsh said emerging technologies will have a significant impact. In the best scenario, productivity and gains are shared broadly and real GDP growth runs persistently above its long-run average. If anticipated investment returns disappoint, the result could be higher unemployment and a slowdown. A Reuters column says the case for accelerating rate hikes is strengthening just as political pressure to go easier has returned.

Tuesday's US data: October import prices are expected at +0.7% m/m (prior +1.1%), retail sales at +0.2% (prior +0.8%) and industrial production at +0.1% (prior +0.7%). Waller, Musalem, Hammack and Williams are scheduled to speak.

Disney (Q4) and Home Depot (Q3) report before the open. Disney is expected to show a revenue jump driven by experiences, with investors watching streaming and cost-savings plans after layoff reports. Home Depot is expected to post higher revenue, with attention on consumer sentiment, the housing market, pricing and annual guidance.

Nike holds its first investor day in nearly a decade and will detail a financial roadmap through 2031. Analysts and shareholders were unimpressed by last month's belt-tightening and want products that win back shoppers from Adidas and Anta.

Biotech and energy M&A: J&J agreed to buy Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.33B ($2.2B upfront). Lilly agreed to buy Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B. Diamondback agreed to buy Double Eagle's Midland Basin units for $5.03B in cash and stock, closing December 21.

Legal and regulatory news: California sued OpenAI over AI-model cyberattacks, including the Hugging Face hack. Intel shareholders filed a class action after a roughly 29% one-day stock drop. Visa and Mastercard are seeking approval of a $38B swipe-fee settlement, and Judge Cogan did not rule at the hearing.

Tesla plans a $3.3B investment in its Gruenheide, Germany gigafactory to build up to 1 million Cybercab robotaxis a year. Construction is to start in the first half of 2027 and production in 2029. The model has yet to be sold at scale anywhere.

Canada's October CPI was 3.1% y/y, unchanged from September and below the 3.2% forecast, with 0.2% m/m. Gasoline rose 30.9% y/y. The TSX fell 1.06% and energy fell 2.11%. Governor Macklem will step down in June 2027. Canadian Natural Resources agreed to buy Advantage Energy for $1.77B including debt.
Reuters notes that safe havens failed to cushion portfolios in recent selloffs, even though investors bought Treasuries and the yen when stocks fell this month.
Trump's meme coin $TRUMP trades near 92 cents, from a 2025 high above $74, ahead of his third crypto gala dinner on November 22.
Warren Buffett is donating about $5.47B of Berkshire Hathaway shares to four charities led by his children and says his confidence in Berkshire is as strong as ever.

market_movers.rationale: Reports Q3 after the close Tuesday, the first update since the CEO's resignation. Investors want to know who will lead the company and whether the AI financing platform continues.
Beat on adjusted EPS (61 cents vs 58 cents) and guided fiscal 2027 adjusted operating income to $1.7B-$2.15B with a meaningful beef improvement. The stock rose 8.74% to $63.96.
Shareholder class action alleges it concealed the impact of slowing PC sales and an inventory glut. It cites a nearly 29% one-day drop and a $23B stock sale at $95 per share in mid-August.
Q4 revenue expected to jump on experiences strength. Streaming slowdown, consumer spending pressure and cost-savings plans are the watch items.
Q3 revenue expected to rise on professional-contractor demand and minor repairs. Investors will look for annual guidance and housing-market commentary.
Investor day lays out a roadmap through 2031 amid falling global sales and investor impatience with the turnaround.
$3.3B Gruenheide investment to produce up to 1 million Cybercabs a year. Production starts in 2029 and the model has not yet been sold at scale.

earnings_insights: NVIDIA Q3, reports after the close Tuesday: LSEG IBES EPS estimate $2.48 (Smart Estimate $2.51) vs $1.30 a year ago, revenue estimate about $109,100.16 mln. Both are estimates, not results. The EPS basis (adjusted or GAAP) is not stated.
The Home Depot Q3, reports before the open Tuesday: EPS estimate $3.84 (Smart Estimate $3.84) vs $3.74 a year ago, revenue estimate $42,791.33 mln (LSEG IBES estimates, not results).
The Walt Disney Company Q4, reports before the open Tuesday: EPS estimate $1.67 (Smart Estimate $1.66) vs $1.11 a year ago, revenue estimate $25,185.82 mln (LSEG IBES estimates, not results).
Tyson Foods Q4 (quarter ended October 3), reported: adjusted EPS 61 cents vs analyst estimate of 58 cents. The beef segment had an adjusted operating loss of $171M vs a $52M loss a year earlier.

Tyson fiscal 2027 guidance: adjusted operating income $1.7B-$2.15B vs $1.98B in fiscal 2026. Revenue is expected to fall 3.5%-5.5% (analysts expected a 1% fall), with plant closures and lower cattle supplies limiting beef volumes. The beef business is guided to between an adjusted loss of $300M and an adjusted income of $100M, vs a $654M loss in 2026.

Bernstein estimates the FAA ground stop cost American, Delta, United and Southwest about $345M pretax combined (80% range $270M-$430M). BofA analysts noted cancellation rates of 22% for American, 28% for JetBlue, 5% for Delta, 3% for United and 4% for Southwest on Sunday.
Nike's investor day on the 2031 financial roadmap follows falling global sales. Analysts are looking for product that wins back share from Adidas and Anta.
